items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So there was Teddy Wilson and that kind of rhythm section playing with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, that they were blowing the bebop stuff.

ctx.x: Because you know, sometimes to understand something you have to be lucky enough to meet someone that you can watch close by what he’s doing. Because there is a human way and a musical way that you can get only just by standing there. And all of a sudden I understood so many more things about music. And we are so used to reason with labels. You know? This is swing, that’s Dixieland, that’s New Orleans, that’s bebop. But if we think of, for example, the early 40s, all the jazz was happening at the same time.…

still around, but Bud Powell and Thelonious Monk, they were starting. So everything was happening at the same time. So there wasn’t a distinction in time like we do today. This was the period that is a way to make it simpler but it does not reflect the reality. So there was Teddy Wilson and that kind of rhythm section playing with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, that they were blowing the bebop stuff. But of course they say that Charlie Parker came from Lester Young. So sometimes I believe that the language…
I liked what you said about physically being next to or behind Barry Harris.
